sources.note: Entry '31. Baan': names Ban-Ogoi, Goi, Ogoi; Rivers State, Gokana-Tai-Eleme LGA, Ban-Ogoi plus villages; <5,000 (1990); Benue-Congo: Cross River: Delta-Cross: Ogoni: Kegboid; dialects Ka-Ban, Kesari. No linguistic description.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2008. The Ogoni languages: comparative word list and historical reconstructions. Draft circulated for comment, printout 13 June 2008, 54 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 3 'Phonology' has one sentence of overview; subsections 3.2-3.6 (incl. '3.6 Baan', p. 5) are empty headings. The Baan column of the wordlist is tone-marked (e.g. boo 'head' with high tones, n-si 'face', to 'ear'), drawn from Nakagawa 1992, Ngulube 2001, N. Williamson n.d. and Ikoro 1989. No statement about stress or tone in prose. Front matter: 'Apart from Tee and Baan, the three other Ogoni languages all have differing dialects' (p. 2).

sources.citation: Bond, Oliver & Gregory D. S. Anderson. 2006. Divergent structure in Ogonoid languages. Proceedings of BLS 31 (Special Session on Languages of West Africa), 13-24. Pre-print version (Word doc 'The Ogonoid-23-03-05', 6 pp, 2-up) from livingtongues.org via the Internet Archive.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent for any Ogonoid language. Only tonal remark: 'Noun class prefixes in Ogonoid, when present, usually carry a low tone or the tone is copied from the initial syllable of the root' (sec. 2.2). Fn. 2: 'Structural data on Baan is almost entirely lacking and as such Baan does not figure heavily into the discussion below.' Sec. 2.1 (coda restrictions) says Baan, like Eleme, has lost all original final consonants 'insofar as this can be determined'.

sources.note: The only located primary phonological description of Baan: a tone-class analysis of verbs from Nakagawa's 1990 fieldwork in Ban-Ogoi. Would establish Baan as a tone language first-hand and may contain a remark on stress/accent. ILCAA back issues are normally in the TUFS repository (tufs.repo.nii.ac.jp), which refused our network (HTTP 406); NDL holds the print volume (ndlsearch R100000001-I11141123635742).
